title: Juicy Canadian Wild Garlic Dumplings
description: A flexitarian-friendly Canadian dish featuring wild garlic leaves, fermented to perfection and steamed in a bamboo steamer, perfect for a weeknight dinner
instructions: In a large mixing bowl, combine flour, yeast, and salt, whisking until well combined.
Gradually add warm water to the dry ingredients, mixing until a shaggy dough forms.
Knead the dough for 10 minutes until it becomes smooth and elastic.
Place the dough in a greased bowl, cover it with a damp cloth, and let it ferment in a warm place for 2 hours.
Prepare the wild garlic leaves by chopping them finely and sauteing them in vegetable oil until fragrant.
Punch down the fermented dough and divide it into small balls, about 1 inch in diameter.
Flatten each ball into a disk shape and place a spoonful of the sauteed wild garlic leaves in the center of each disk.
Fold the dough over the filling to form a half-moon shape and press the edges together to seal the dumpling.
Place the dumplings in a bamboo steamer lined with parchment paper, leaving some space between each dumpling.
Steam the dumplings over boiling water for 15 minutes, or until they are cooked through and fluffy.
Serve the dumplings hot with a dipping sauce made from soy sauce and rice vinegar.
